messages:
devon: customer (acct 4321) hit us after yesterday's egress hardening — intermittent TLS failures to our private inference endpoint. errors: 'tls: handshake failure' and client sees 'x509: certificate is valid for internal.cluster, not inference.redwood.example'. they only started after we tightened firewall rules.
maria: yikes. any repro steps from the customer?
kevin: they sent a curl trace, here's the important bits: ```curl -v --resolve inference.redwood.example:443:10.2.4.5 https://inference.redwood.example/health --trace-ascii -``` shows TLS ClientHello -> Server Hello -> then client resets after about 3s. also saw intermittent DNS resolving to 10.2.4.5 (internal) instead of front-door IP.
support-engineer: they are on a private VPC, split-horizon DNS in their onprem resolver returns internal LB IP. when we probe from our side we get the public IP. could be a middlebox rewriting or blocking ephemeral return ports.
kevin: ran tcpdump on a repro host (filtered): ```14:02:11.123456 IP 10.10.1.22.49160 > 10.2.4.5.443: Flags [S], seq 0
14:02:11.124001 IP 10.2.4.5.443 > 10.10.1.22.49160: Flags [S.], seq 0 ack 1
14:02:14.130000 IP 10.10.1.22.49160 > 10.2.4.5.443: Flags [R], seq 1 ack 1
``` RST comes from client side after SYN/ACK, suggests some middlebox saw TLS/SNI mismatch or connection state timed out.
devon: can you paste their NACL/SG egress rules? asking if ephemeral range is allowed.
maria: they attached screenshots: SG outbound only allows 443 to 10.2.4.0/24, and NACL has a DENY rule ordering that denies 49152-65535 (rule 110) before the allow for 0-65535 (rule 200) — looks like an accidental explicit block.
support-engineer: aha. that would drop return traffic when source port falls in that range. TCP handshake shows SYN/SYN-ACK but client RST after delay — conntrack on client likely lost state then RST. also their DNS split-horizon means cert presented by our public front-door doesn't match the IP they connect to; if there's an SNI-inspecting proxy it could reject early.
kevin: command I used to validate from their subnet: ```nc -vz -w 5 10.2.4.5 443``` got "succeeded" intermittently then long pause then RST. changed local firewall to allow ephemeral ports (32768-61000) and issue stopped.
devon: good catch. action plan: 1) ask customer to remove the explicit DENY for ephemeral range in their NACL or move it after allow rules, 2) verify split-horizon DNS maps to our public edge if they expect public cert, or update certs to cover internal LB name, 3) advise to whitelist our front-door IPs in SG if they want direct path.
maria: I'll draft a support KB with minimal repro steps and commands to share. include tcpdump snippet and recommendation to check NACL rule ordering + ephemeral port ranges.
infra-bot: ticket #SUP-2026 created for follow-up and config checklist attached. :white_check_mark:
support-engineer: customer confirmed after removing the DENY rule and allowing ephemeral range the handshakes succeeded and no more cert mismatch errors reported (they also fixed DNS to point to public edge). closing for now, will reopen if it recurs. :slightly_smiling_face:
